text:
alex: Heads up — noticed a 12-20% host-side p99 regression on streaming requests after the recent kernel-selection tweak. Looks concentrated in parse/tokenize and small-write paths.

maria: Where's the profile? Can you paste the flame/trace?

alex: trace: https://perf.redwood/s/trace-abc123 — flame points to heavy CPU in `parse_frame` -> `serialize_prefix` and lots of `writev` syscalls.

jon: Is this gRPC framing or HTTP2? writev spikes usually come from gRPC's small-chunk writes.

alex: Mostly gRPC, yes. Repro script I used: `scripts/repro_stream.sh --rate 200 --seq-len 512` (local loadgen).

lisa: Also seeing KV cache miss rate spike correlated with the same timeframe — kv_miss_rate +3.2x on the canary hosts.

ryan: The kernel-selection change picked `quant_opt_v2` kernels for the model family. Those kernels add an extra prepack/serialize stage for KV prefixes — might explain the memcpy overhead.

alex: Exactly. The new path calls `serialize_prefix` which allocates and copies into a temp buffer per request. That plus fragmented writes is killing the p99.

maria: Quick diagnostic: can you force the old kernel path with env `RW_KERNEL=legacy` and rerun the repro?

alex: Testing now... switched to `RW_KERNEL=legacy` on canary. Re-ran script: p99 returned to baseline (within noise). So kernel path is likely the culprit.

jon: We shouldn't rollback wholesale. Two options: 1) mend the kernel path to avoid extra memcpy; 2) adjust batching/coalescing heuristics on host to amortize the extra cost.

ryan: Agreed. Coalescing small writes into 4k-aligned buffers before writev reduced syscall overhead in past incidents. Also consider bumping the batching horizon by ~1-2ms for streaming clients to give the runtime a chance to assemble larger writes.

alex: I've put up PR #3456: skip redundant memcpy in `serialize_prefix` and add a `small_write_coalesce` step (in host preproc) that aggregates sub-4k frames. Local bench: p95 -6%, p99 -14% vs the broken kernel path.

ci-bot: CI run for PR #3456: host-parse perf test shows p99 improvement -13.7% vs canary-broken (run 2026-03-20T10:12Z). Full unit/integration passed.

lisa: Nice. Can we also add a guard in KV cache logic? The miss spike looked like a rehashing pattern triggered by changed prefix shapes. Pin hot shards or add small LRU-prefetch.

alex: Opened follow-up PR #3457 to add an LRU prefetch for hot shard keys and a short pin window for hot prefixes. Preliminary local: kv_miss_rate down ~45% under repro.

maria: Plan for rollout: canary PR #3456 + #3457 to 10% traffic tomorrow morning, monitor p99, kv_miss_rate, writev_calls, and writev_bytes_per_call. If stable for 2h, bump to 50% then 100%.

jon: Also add a short-term metric: `host.writev.small_calls_ratio` (calls <4k) and an alert if it increases >10% over baseline during rollout.

alex: Will add metrics + dashboard.

maria: Thx — @ryan @jon please review PRs and we can schedule the canary.

ci-bot: Deployment check: canary infra quota ok for 10% tomorrow window.

alex: Pushing changelog/bench logs to the PRs. Will post full flame and raw pprof diffs after the next repro. :thumbsup:
